situation:
You are the market planning manager for HOLLOW CREEK FESTIVAL COMPANY, a family business now in its third generation, which produces a four-day music festival every summer on leased county fairgrounds. The president (judge) is the grandchild of the founder, has run the festival for eleven years, and has kept every booking decision inside the family for all of them.

The festival sells out its twelve thousand tickets within a day of going on sale, and the grounds cannot safely hold more people than that. Demand has run well ahead of the seats available for four straight summers, resale prices climb every year, and the company collects nothing from those resales. The aging stage also limits which touring acts will accept a date at all.

The county has offered to pay half the cost of a new amphitheater on the grounds, on the condition that the company bring in an experienced operating partner. MERIDIAN LIVE, a national concert promoter, will supply the other half and guarantee the company a fixed annual payment. In exchange, MERIDIAN LIVE books the headline acts and sets the dates, so the family stops choosing the lineup that made the festival regional in character.

The company can instead fund the amphitheater alone, out of its reserves and a bank loan, and keep the booking decisions in the family. Paying for it that way takes most of the next several summers' ticket revenue, leaves the stage as it is for another two seasons, and sends the county's half to a rival festival one valley over that has asked for the same money.

The president (judge) wants your reading of where the festival stands and a recommendation on which path the company should take, including what each one does to the festival's competitive advantage. The president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of HOLLOW CREEK FESTIVAL COMPANY. Business background is the same as the situation above.

Your grandparent started this festival on a borrowed flatbed stage, and you have run it for eleven years without an outside partner in the business. You want to hear where the market planning manager thinks the festival stands, which path is recommended, and what the festival looks like some years after that recommendation has been in force.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Three summers from now, what does this decision look like?
What would you watch for to know it had gone wrong?
